job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our Class 7 science lab at Delhi Public School, Mr. Sharma organized a fascinating experiment to observe water movement in plants. He placed a fresh white carnation in a beaker filled with 200 ml of water mixed with red ink. On October 12, Rahul and Priya watched the petals closely for three hours. By the end of the session, the white petals turned red because the stem absorbed the colored water through tiny tubes called xylem. Mr. Sharma explained that this process is similar to how blood travels through our veins. While Rohan suggested that the ink moves because the petals are thirsty, Mr. Sharma clarified that the movement happens due to transpiration pull from the leaves. Later, the students recorded that 15 leaves were attached to the main stem. This experiment shows that plants have a transport system just like animals. It is not because the petals are alive, but because the xylem acts like a straw. Even though the beaker held 200 ml, only a small amount was pulled up into the flower. The students learned that plants need a continuous supply of water to survive, much like how animals need a heart to pump blood.
response.summary: Students conducted an experiment using red ink to observe how plants transport water through their stems. The activity demonstrated that xylem tubes move water upward, similar to how blood circulates in animals.
